title: New Methods for Constructing Classical and Quantum Codes from Graphs and Matroids
authors: Anderson S. Barbosa, Franklin de L. Marquezino, Giuliano G. La Guardia
abstract: In this paper, we present a method for constructing linear codes derived from book graphs. Applying such a method, we construct binary codes that have the greatest possible minimum distance for their length and dimension by means of the $2$-sum of two equal book graphs. We then utilize matroid and graph theory together to investigate some properties of the resulting linear codes. Furthermore, we show that, from the incidence matrix of any graph, we can obtain a linear code over any finite field maintaining the same parameters. Furthermore, we show how the condition for two linear codes to generate a Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code translates into matroid theory and, utilizing cycle graphs, we exhibit a way to generate codes that meet this condition.
summary: This paper develops a powerful theoretical framework to construct both classical and quantum error-correcting codes using the mathematical tools of graph theory and matroid theory. By analyzing structures like book graphs and employing the 2-sum operation, the authors demonstrate methods to generate codes with provably optimal minimum distances. This work provides new, graph-theoretic pathways for designing robust quantum codes.
main_problem: The paper focuses on constructing efficient linear and quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs) by establishing deep connections between coding theory, graph theory, and matroid theory.
main_result: The authors present methods to construct binary codes with maximum minimum distance using the 2-sum of book graphs, and they show how to generate quantum CSS codes using matroid theory.
method: The core method involves translating code construction problems into the language of matroids, utilizing graph operations like the 2-sum, and relating code properties to the incidence matrices of graphs.
model_or_system: The underlying mathematical structures are classical and quantum error-correcting codes (ECCs and QECCs). The construction is based on graph theory (book graphs, cycle graphs) and matroid theory.
key_observables: Code parameters such as length ($n$), dimension ($k$), and minimum Hamming distance ($d$) for both classical and quantum codes.
important_parameters: The field over which the code is defined ($\mathbb{F}_q$), the structure of the underlying graphs (e.g., book graphs), and the type of code (e.g., CSS code).
main_assumptions: The construction relies on specific properties of matroids, such as the relationship between circuits and the null space of the incidence matrix, and the structure of the 2-sum operation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the graphical construction of graph operations like the parallel connection and 2-sum, and Figure 4 displays the generator matrices for four constructed binary codes.
paper_structure: The paper develops foundational theorems relating matroids to linear codes, details graph operations (parallel connection, 2-sum), and culminates in applying these tools to construct specific, high-performance classical and quantum codes.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting graph structures directly to the construction of optimal quantum error-correcting codes is highly relevant for theoretical quantum information scientists.
